text:
incident-bot: PAGER — Severity: S2 — Observed sudden p99 latency spike on streaming endpoints (/v1/stream and /v1/generate) starting ~09:12 UTC. Affected region: us-west-2. Current p95: 420ms (ok), p99: 4.2s (breach). Estimated impacted requests: ~2.5k/min. Paging on-call SRE.

sre_ash: ack, I'm on it. pulling up traces and tail logs now. tagging infra/maya for hardware checks. @infra_maya can you grab GPU node health for the cluster handling streaming pool A?

infra_maya: on it. looking at node set gpupool-a-*. Initial glance: one host (gpupool-a-17) showing rising GPU temp and correctable ECC counters. nvtop and metrics show thermal throttle flags toggling. sending `nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE,THERMAL,FB_ERRORS` now.

sre_ash: thanks. eng-runtime-john, any recent deploys or config changes to the streaming runtime in the last 30m?

eng-runtime-john: no deploys in the last hour. We did push a small batching tweak yesterday but nothing on the runtime path. Metrics look like a per-node tail; streaming stalls correspond to spikes in kernel-scheduling wait. also seeing backlog of KV cache misses around the same timestamps.

ops_lina: customer-facing queues show retries increased; streaming sessions are either timing out or re-established with longer latencies. CS Rafael heads-up: we should prepare a quick note for the top impacted customers.

cust_success_rafael: preparing templated message now. will hold until we know if this is degraded or partial outage. please flag any customers with high SLA exposure: enterprise tenants on dedicated nodes.

sre_ash: pasted nv-smi snippet:
```
# gpupool-a-17 nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE,THERMAL,FB_ERRORS
GPU 0:
    Temperature : 93 C
    Performance State : P2
    Throttle Reasons : thermal, application
    FB Memory Errors (Corrected) : 142
    ECC Errors (Corrected) : 347
```

infra_maya: ECC correctables trending upward rapidly over last 15m — suggests flaky memory subsystem or intermittent power/thermal issue. node also shows GPU clock drops -> thermal throttle. I'm going to cordon and start evacuation if we see continued p99.

sre_ash: agree. plan proposal (short term):
- mark gpupool-a-17 as DRAIN (evacuate new sessions)
- re-route 100% new streams off the host via routing rules
- initiate immediate live fallback: enable model variant fallback to quantized v2 for streaming in this pool (lower perf but avoids stalls)
- trigger graceful drain of active sessions on node for 5 minutes with sticky reconnect to other hosts
- notify customers for potential degraded latency

eng-runtime-john: adding: also drop `continuous_batch_size` by 20% for the pool to reduce kernel contention while drain is happening. starting a canary of fallback config to 25% first.

deploy-bot: Rollout: update-route /streaming -> set fallback_variant=quant-v2 (canary 25%) initiated by eng-runtime-john at 09:21 UTC. Tracking: rollout-id r-799123-a

sre_ash: executing drain: `infractl nodes drain gpupool-a-17 --grace-period 300 --evacuate-sessions` (running)

infra_maya: drain command returned OK, sessions being rebalanced. I also kicked a soft reboot of the host's BMC to stabilize thermal sensors while we evacuate. hw ticket created: HW-799123 (for board replacement if needed).

ops_lina: internal dashboard shows p99 dropping from 4.2s -> 1.1s in the next 90s after routing change and canary. Still seeing intermittent 2s spikes on long streaming sessions that were pinned.

sre_ash: good. continuing to monitor. pulling KV cache hit rates: they spiked miss ratio from 2% -> 18% at start, now down to 6% as sessions move. suspecting node-level stalls caused cache lookup backpressure.

eng-runtime-john: i'm lowering batch size for gpupool-a quanta and bumping concurrency limiter for streaming connections to avoid head-of-line blocking. applying change now: `rtctl update pool gpupool-a --batch-mult=0.8 --stream-concurrency=80%`.

platform-sean: FYI, autoscaler logs show a temporary surge of small worker starts to compensate which might cause transient cold caches — we should watch cost but it's preventing hard errors.

cust_success_rafael: sent initial notice to 3 impacted enterprise customers: short note saying we saw elevated streaming latencies, mitigation in progress, ETA 30-45m. clients asked to contact support if they see errors.

sre_ash: status update 09:28 UTC: p99 at 900ms, p95 stable. No customer-facing error-rate spike (5xxs) beyond normal. Evacuation progress: 84% sessions migrated off gpupool-a-17. Continuing to drain; if ECC correctables keep climbing we escalate to replace GPU.

infra_maya: ECC counters paused growth after soft reboot but temps still borderline (88-92C). I'm scheduling a full cold-reboot and hardware replacement window; marking node as quarantined for now. HW ticket updated HW-799123 -> escalated.

ops_lina: CS confirms no immediate SLAs breached for the notified customers, but they flagged a large batch job that might be sensitive to tail latency — shared mitigation steps.

sre_ash: moving to handoff: i'm going AFK in 20m. @infra_maya please take incident lead for hardware remediation and oncall for next hour. @eng-runtime-john you'll own follow-up for runtime config and postmortem items. @cust_success_rafael continue customer comms.

infra_maya: taking lead. I'll finish quarantine, run `memtest` and schedule GPU RMA if memtest/thermal persists. also will coordinate capacity swap for dedicated tenants if needed.

eng-runtime-john: noted. I'll capture config diffs and the rollout snapshot (r-799123-a) and prepare a regression test to ensure fallback doesn't cause regressions. will also add a metric to detect GPU thermal throttle spikes earlier.

sre_ash: one more note — we saw streaming stalls mostly on requests > 2k tokens where KV cache and GPU memory pressure spikes. for postmortem: correlate long-tail tokens + batch scheduling to see if we can proactively fall back earlier for long sessions.

platform-sean: opened follow-up ticket PLAT-799124 to add thermal-throttle alert at host-level with 3-min smoothing and auto-evacuate playbook link.

cust_success_rafael: customers acknowledged, one asked for postmortem and ETA for fix. I said we'll provide within 48h.

infra_maya: final infra action now: host gpupool-a-17 set QUARANTINED, drain completed. scheduling offload and replacement. I'll keep incident channel updated.

sre_ash: closing actionable incident notes — immediate mitigation succeeded: routing + canary fallback + drain. Impact: p99 improved from 4.2s -> 0.9s, no sustained 5xx increase, affected customers notified. Next: HW replace, add earlier throttle alert, and investigate kernel scheduling interactions on long streaming sessions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — Severity reduced to S3 at 09:41 UTC. Incident will remain open for postmortem tracking. Incident channel owner: infra_maya.

infra_maya: handing off to oncall for monitoring through the night. leaving detailed runbook steps in the ticket (HW-799123). I'll update with RMA ETA.

eng-runtime-john: prepping short-term config revert if fallback rollout causes quality regressions. i'll attach eval diffs to the postmortem.

cust_success_rafael: scheduling customer postmortem email after root cause analysis. will coordinate with eng-runtime-john for exact wording.

sre_ash: thanks team. leaving final note: good coordination on routing and evacuation. please add any additional actions in the follow-up tickets: HW-799123, PLAT-799124, RT-799125.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for active paging at 09:59 UTC. Please file postmortem in /incidents/postmortems when ready.
